content_voiceover: This is the QuANTUM-First trial design, and it's the reason quizartinib now has a frontline indication. Enrolled patients had newly diagnosed FLT3-ITD positive AML, with at least 3 percent ITD allelic frequency, ages 18 to 75, total of 539 patients. They were stratified by region, age above or below 60, and baseline white count above or below 40, then randomized 1 to 1 on day 7 of cycle 1, plus or minus 3 days. Both arms got standard 7 plus 3 induction, cytarabine days 1 through 7 with daunorubicin or idarubicin days 1 through 3, for up to 2 cycles. Starting day 8, one arm added quizartinib and the other placebo. Consolidation was up to 4 cycles of high dose cytarabine with quizartinib or placebo, and allo transplant was allowed per institutional policy. Responders then moved into a continuation phase, single agent quizartinib or placebo once daily, for up to 36 cycles, essentially maintenance therapy.
keypoints: FLT3-ITD positive AML, N equals 539, randomized 1 to 1
Induction and consolidation add quizartinib or placebo to standard chemo
Continuation phase gives single agent quizartinib or placebo up to 36 cycles
Allo-HSCT permitted during consolidation per institutional policy
keypoint_voiceover: Key points here. This is FLT3-ITD positive AML, 539 patients randomized 1 to 1. Quizartinib or placebo is layered onto standard induction and consolidation chemotherapy. And critically, responders go on to a long continuation phase of single agent quizartinib or placebo for up to 36 cycles, which functions as maintenance. Allo transplant was allowed during consolidation per local practice.
